use: Only the date; a length of one day is ichinichi.

example.romaji: raigetsu no tsuitachi ni hikkosu n da.
example.ja: 来月の一日に引っ越すんだ。
example.english: I'm moving on the 1st of next month.

examplePolite.ja: 来月の一日に引っ越します。
examplePolite.english: I'm moving on the 1st of next month.

use: Same word for the date and for a two-day span.

example.romaji: shigatsu futsuka ga tanjoubi nan da.
example.ja: 四月二日が誕生日なんだ。

examplePolite.ja: 四月二日が誕生日です。

example.english: I think it'll be done in three days.

examplePolite.ja: 三日で終わると思います。
examplePolite.english: I think it will be finished in three days.

example.english: How about the afternoon of the 4th?

examplePolite.romaji: yokka no gogo wa ikaga desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 四日の午後はいかがですか？
examplePolite.english: Would the afternoon of the 4th work?

notes: Don't mix with youka (the 8th): yokka has the short pause, youka the long o.

examplePolite.ja: 五日までに教えてください。
examplePolite.english: Please let me know by the 5th.

notes: Sounds the same as itsuka (someday); context tells them apart.

example.english: I'm on a business trip until the 6th.

examplePolite.english: I'm away on business until the 6th.

example.english: Are you free the night of the 7th?

examplePolite.romaji: nanoka no yoru wa aite imasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 七日の夜は空いていますか？
examplePolite.english: Are you free on the evening of the 7th?

example.romaji: youka made ni henji suru ne.
example.ja: 八日までに返事するね。
example.english: I'll get back to you by the 8th.

examplePolite.ja: 八日までに返事します。

example.romaji: kokonoka wa tomodachi no kekkonshiki nan da.
example.ja: 九日は友達の結婚式なんだ。

examplePolite.romaji: kokonoka wa tomodachi no kekkonshiki desu.
examplePolite.ja: 九日は友達の結婚式です。

use: Like the 4th it takes yokka, not yonnichi.

example.romaji: barentain wa nigatsu juuyokka da yo.
example.ja: バレンタインは二月十四日だよ。

examplePolite.ja: バレンタインは二月十四日です。

example.ja: 二十日に家賃払わなきゃ。
example.english: I have to pay rent on the 20th.

examplePolite.romaji: hatsuka ni yachin o harawanai to ikemasen.
examplePolite.ja: 二十日に家賃を払わないといけません。
examplePolite.english: I have to pay the rent on the 20th.

use: Any date ending in 4 uses yokka: 4th, 14th, 24th.

example.romaji: nijuuyokka no yoru wa dou suru?
example.ja: 二十四日の夜はどうする？
example.english: What are you doing the night of the 24th?

examplePolite.romaji: nijuuyokka no yoru wa dou shimasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 二十四日の夜はどうしますか？
examplePolite.english: What are your plans for the evening of the 24th?

name: Regular dates
formation: number + -nichi: juuichinichi (11th), juusannichi (13th), juushichinichi (17th), juukunichi (19th), sanjuunichi (30th), sanjuuichinichi (31st)
use: Every date not on the irregular list is just the number plus nichi; 17th and 19th use shichi and ku.

example.ja: 十五日から夏休みだよ。

examplePolite.ja: 十五日から夏休みです。

example.english: What date will the meeting be?

examplePolite.romaji: kaigi wa nannichi ni narimasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 会議は何日になりますか？
examplePolite.english: What date will the meeting be on?

notes: Add -kan to ask only the length: nannichikan.

use: Takes the irregular day forms: futsukakan, mikkakan, yokkakan, tookakan; one day is ichinichi, not tsuitachi.

example.ja: 三日間ずっと雨だった。
example.english: It rained for three days straight.

examplePolite.ja: 三日間ずっと雨でした。
examplePolite.english: It rained for three days straight.

notes: -kan is often dropped: mikka yasunda (took three days off).

english: one day; a day (per day); a whole day
use: A length of one day; the date 'the 1st' is tsuitachi.

example.english: How many hours a day do you sleep?

examplePolite.ja: 一日に何時間寝ますか？
examplePolite.english: How many hours a day do you sleep?

examplePolite.ja: 昨日は一日中寝ていました。

use: A bit formal; in casual talk people often say nisannichi (two or three days).

example.english: They said it'll heal in a few days.

examplePolite.english: I'm told it will heal in a few days.
